reason: Two rx_run.js processes ran concurrently and appended to the same JSONL files. An earlier `nohup ... &` launch started a process despite its output redirect failing, and a second process was later launched via the background task runner. Both wrote to runs/afexRX/.
what_is_still_valid: Each individual row's `nodes` field is a genuine measurement of afExists for that (E,A); duplication does not corrupt individual measurements.
capped.jsonl is correct and demonstrates the preregistered fail-closed rule working: eIndex 12 rank 66 hit the 5e6 cap and the automatic 2e9 recheck resolved it AF-negative in 6,483,407 nodes.
Per-E mean node costs extracted from this run were used only as a cost model, never as a result.
what_is_NOT_valid: All counts: trials, afPositive, per-E totals. Duplicated and partial.
All timings in afexRX.stdout: the log interleaves two processes with different start times, so elapsed figures are meaningless.

second_defect_found.issue: persist.js Appender calls fs.fsyncSync after every record. rx_run.js wrote one record per trial (~75k fsyncs), where Report 7's af_exists_run.js persisted only AF-positive rows (202 and 58). Per-record fsync, compounded by two processes contending on the same files, dominated runtime: ~640 ms/trial observed against ~45 ms/trial expected from node counts.
second_defect_found.fix: Re-run as a single process with an exclusive lock, persisting AF-positive and capped rows with fsync (few) and the per-trial audit log through a buffered stream flushed at each E boundary.

note: No preregistered parameter changed. Quota Q=5000, AF cap 5e6, recheck cap 2e9, ordering rule and decision rules are all unchanged. Only the I/O implementation and process management changed.
